files.purpose: Holds every piece of the software-update story shown on the Settings About page: a parser that turns a GitLab release description into three categorised sections (UpdateReleaseNotesDigest with ReleaseNoteCategory New features / Bug fixes / Refinements), the three tinted tappable cards and their bullet popovers, and the About chrome accessory made of an identity pill (app icon plus "v<version>") and a version pill that is either a status seal (Up to date / Check failed / Not checked yet), the blue "Update & restart" button, or an animated install progress slider. It also contains the frame-driven progress slider itself (an exponential chase of the download fraction, a blue gradient fill revealed by a leading clip, 14 deterministic twinkling sparkles seeded by SplitMix64 and a white head), the unread UpdateAvailableDot, the AboutSoftwareUpdateSection that runs a check when the page opens and plays the post-relaunch celebration sweep with haptics, and the AboutUpdateCheckRow with its "Check now" button and relative last-checked text.

They are drawn after `context.clip(to: reveal)` and `context.opacity = opacity` (lines 461-462), so they appear only inside the revealed fill and are multiplied by the fill fade-in opacity. feature_notes:
Notes parsing (lines 103-105): `for line in raw.split(separator: "
", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)` keeps empty lines; each line is `line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)` (Foundation CharacterSet.whitespaces: Unicode general category Zs plus tab, not newlines); lines that are empty, exactly "---", or start with "<" are skipped. Swift Character rule: the separator is the Character "
", and "
" is a single grapheme Character that does not equal "
", so notes with CRLF line endings do not split at all. They arrive as one line; if it starts with "## New features
..." category(forHeader:) (line 153) fails because the lowercased text is not an exact match, isHeader (line 142) is true, current = nil (line 117), nothing is collected, the digest is empty and releaseBody (lines 749-754) falls back to the raw MarkdownView. A port using JS split("
") plus trim() (which also strips ) would show cards for the same notes; to match B2 it must not split on "
".

A bullet is a line whose first character is one of - U+2010 U+2013 U+2014 U+2212 * • followed by a space or tab, with a non-empty trimmed body. Bullets before any recognised section header are dropped. Each bullet has inline markdown stripped (links [text](url) -> text, **bold** -> bold, `code` -> code, applied in that order) and is kept only if non-empty.

A non-bullet line that names a category sets the current section, whether bare or with # heading or ** bold chrome, trailing spaces/tabs/colons trimmed; matching is case-insensitive: "new features" or "new" -> New features; "bug fixes", "fixes" or "bugs" -> Bug fixes; "refinements" or "improvements" -> Refinements.

Any other heading (one or more # followed by space/tab or nothing, or a line that starts and ends with ** and is longer than 4 characters) closes the current section (current = nil), so e.g. a Thanks to contributors section is left out. Plain text lines that are neither leave the current section unchanged.
Sections are emitted in the fixed order New features, Bug fixes, Refinements; empty or missing ones are absent. Bullets are de-duplicated case-insensitively keeping the first occurrence.

Rollup: if the last kept bullet contains a word equal to "extra" (lowercased, punctuation trimmed) that is not the first word, and the preceding word's digit characters parse to an Int > 0, that bullet becomes the section's rollup and its number is rollupCount ("Fixed 12 extra issues…" counts as 12). changeCount = bullets.count + rollupCount.
parse(nil) or parse("") returns an empty digest; parse memoizes the last (raw, digest) pair and returns the cached digest when raw is identical.
The page re-parses only when checker.update?.version changes (.onChange(..., initial: true)). If the digest is empty but the notes are not, the raw notes are rendered as Markdown instead of cards.
Card tap toggles its popover (tapping the open card closes it); a card with no section does nothing and is disabled.

FractionChase: the first advance snaps displayed to target; a target below displayed snaps back down; dt is clamped to [0, 0.25] s; step = remaining * (1 - exp(-dt / max(response, 0.01))), then at least minimumSpeed * dt, capped at the target; within 0.0001 of the target it snaps to the target.

SmoothedUpdateProgressSlider frame clock runs at up to 60 fps and pauses when settled (displayed fraction == target) or while ScrollActivity reports scrolling; settled resets to false whenever target.value changes. The chase is created caught up to target.value so a post-relaunch sweep does not start from zero.

Head x = trackHeight/2 + (width - trackHeight) * clamp(value, 0, 1). Fill opacity is 0 at or below 0.012, 1 at or above 0.05, smoothstep t*t*(3-2t) in between. The fill is revealed by a rounded clip of width max(headX, trackHeight/2) and corner radius height/2.

Sparkle motion: twinkle = 0.5 + 0.5*sin(time*speed + phase); horizontal drift = sin(time*speed*0.31 + phase*2.1) * drift; sparkle canvas runs at up to 30 fps and pauses when there are no sparkles or while scrolling.

SparkleParticle.field uses SplitMix64: state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9; z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB; z ^= z >> 31; value = Double(z >> 11) / 2^53. Per particle the draws are in order x = r, y = 0.12 + r*0.76, size = 1.2 + r*1.6, speed = 0.9 + r*2.4, phase = r*2π, drift = 0.6 + r*1.4. Seed 0x5EED_D80B, count 14.

Version pill logic: isReady = checker.updateAvailable && checker.update != nil && !progress.showsProgressUI. Standing precedence: lastError != nil -> failed; else lastCheckedAt == nil -> unchecked; else upToDate. While installing, slider response is 0.15 with reduce motion, else 0.72 while phase == .celebrating, else 0.3; minimumSpeed is 0.12 while celebrating, else 0.

Standing tooltips verbatim: upToDate "Droppy Code <AppInfo.version> is the latest version"; failed = checker.lastError, or "The last check did not reach GitLab"; unchecked "Droppy Code has not asked GitLab for a release yet".

releaseDetail (lines 781-791) joins with " · ": "Released <date, .long, no time>" when releasedAt exists, then `ByteCountFormatStyle(style: .file).format(size)` when size exists, then always "Update & restart installs it in place and relaunches." The .file style output is decided by Foundation, not this file: Apple documents the .file count style as the platform file-size style, which on macOS is the decimal (1000-based) style, e.g. "12.3 MB" for about 12,300,000 bytes, not 1024-based. A Windows port must format with 1000-based units (not StrFormatByteSize, which is 1024-based) and pin the exact digits and locale from a macOS sample.

Celebration sweep (startCelebrationSweep, lines 795-818): first `celebration?.cancel()` cancels any earlier sweep, then `let reduceMotion = reduceMotion` snapshots reduce motion once when the sweep starts (a later change to reduce motion does not affect a sweep already running); then in a @MainActor Task: wait 550 ms; abort unless !Task.isCancelled and progress.phase == .celebrating; finishCelebrationSweep(); with reduce motion: haptic .alignment then 900 ms; otherwise 900 ms, haptic .alignment, 450 ms, haptic .levelChange, 700 ms (cancellation checked between steps); then completeCelebration(). Leaving the page mid-sweep completes the celebration at once.

Check row detail verbatim: while checking "Asking GitLab for the latest release…"; otherwise checked = "Checked <relative named date>." or "Not checked yet."; with an error "<error> <checked>"; with a ready update "Droppy Code <version> is ready to install. <checked>"; otherwise "Droppy Code checks GitLab for new versions a few times a day. <checked>".

B1->B2: (1) strippedInlineMarkdown no longer uses three cached NSRegularExpression statics (linkPattern, boldPattern, codePattern) with a stripped(_:with:) helper and "$1" template; it now uses Swift Regex literals with String.replacing and the first capture, same three patterns in the same order, doc comment says it is cheap because parse memoizes. (2) Fixed-point fonts switched to system text styles: card count size 11 -> .subheadline; popover title size 13 semibold -> .body semibold; popover version size 11 -> .subheadline; bullets size 13 -> .body; rollup size 12 -> .callout; identity pill version size 12 semibold -> .callout semibold; both version pill titles size 12 semibold -> .callout semibold; Release notes link size 12 medium -> .callout medium and its arrow size 10 semibold -> .footnote semibold. (3) Popover colours changed: version text .tertiary -> Chrome.secondaryText, bullets .secondary -> Chrome.secondaryText, rollup .tertiary -> Chrome.secondaryText. The card title stays .system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium). File shrank from 852 to 845 lines; no strings, logic or timings changed.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: the point sizes the text styles .subheadline, .body, .callout, .footnote resolve to on macOS are not stated in this file (Apple's macOS defaults are commonly 11, 13, 12, 10); the Windows port must pin them from a runtime measurement or the Chrome/design source, not assume.

Chrome.capsuleHorizontalPadding, capsuleVerticalPadding, capsuleContentHeight, inlineIconFont, sectionSpacing, the chromeGlassCapsule and presentedChrome modifiers are defined elsewhere; values not in this file.

How often the checker actually polls (the text says "a few times a day") and what UpdateInstallProgress.showsProgressUI / fractionTarget / phase values are come from UpdateChecker and UpdateInstallProgress, not this file.

Where AboutUpdateCheckRow and AboutUpdateChromeAccessory are placed on screen is decided by the Settings/About views, not this file. UpdateAvailableDot is placed per its own doc comment (line 526) "on the Settings row and the About row while a release waits" (B2 uses it at SettingsView.swift:161 and SidebarView.swift:171).
The exact Haptics.perform(.alignment/.levelChange) feedback has no direct Windows equivalent; the Windows substitute needs an adaptation decision.

files.purpose: Renders the Hydra pairs cookbook, a fixed 460x540 panel opened as a popover from the Hydra settings page's Pairs section. It resolves every HydraCookbook recipe against the current provider registry and settings, lists the recipes that resolve to a concrete HydraPair as ready rows each with a one-click Add button (or an "Added" label once the pair is in settings), and lists recipes whose provider is not set up under a dimmed "Needs a provider" heading. When the panel appears it loads the model catalog of every ready provider so recipes can pick their models.

files.purpose: Builds the Settings page for Hydra, the feature where one chat leads a team of helper "heads": a hero card with the master hydraEnabled switch, then sections for Heads, Messages, When the team is done and Pairs that all dim to 0.5 opacity and disable while Hydra is off, and an always-enabled informational Where heads run section. It binds a dozen AppSettings hydra* flags to ChromeRow toggles, visual pickers and a segmented head-cap picker, lists the configured HydraPairs with a hover edit affordance and a remove button, and adds pairs by picking the first installed and enabled provider without a pair yet. The file also contains the HydraPairEditor popover that edits a pair's name, lead provider, model and effort, heads provider, model and effort, and heads-at-once cap, with rules that reset dependent fields when the provider or model changes and loads provider catalogs on demand.

Changing lead provider (only if different): inside model.updateHydraPair `guard $0.provider != provider else { return }`; sets provider, clears orchestratorModel and orchestratorEffort; if workerProvider == nil clears workerModel and workerEffort; else if workerProvider == new provider sets workerProvider = nil. `Task { await registry.loadCatalog(provider) }` (line 405) sits outside the update closure, so it runs whenever the binding setter is called, including a re-pick of the same provider where the guard made the edit a no-op (whether GlassPickerButton calls the setter on a re-pick is decided in GlassPickerButton, not this file).

Changing lead model: sets orchestratorModel; clears orchestratorEffort if the new model option exists and does not list that effort. Same rule for the heads model and workerEffort against headsProvider.

Changing heads provider: inside the update closure `let chosen = provider == $0.provider ? nil : provider` then `guard $0.workerProvider != chosen else { return }`; otherwise sets workerProvider = chosen and clears workerModel and workerEffort. Outside the closure `if let provider { Task { await registry.loadCatalog(provider) } }` (line 455) loads the raw picked provider, not `chosen`, and runs even when the guard returned early (it would also run for a provider equal to the lead, though the options at line 443 exclude pair.provider). catalogProviders(pair) = [provider, headsProvider] when sendsHeadsElsewhere else [provider]; the editor's .task keyed on it loads each catalog in order.

files.purpose: Implements the floating 380-point-wide panel where a user enters an MCP connector's key or other fields. MCPKeyPanel is a @MainActor singleton that opens the catalog entry's keysURL in the default browser, hosts MCPKeyPanelView in a borderless-looking non-activating floating NSPanel placed 24 points in from the top-right of the main screen's visible frame, and closes it on its own xmark, on Escape through a local key-down monitor, or once the connector reports connected. MCPKeyPanelView shows numbered steps, one monospaced text, secure or path field per MCPField (paths chosen with an NSOpenPanel), and a Save and connect or Sign in button that is enabled only when the MCP manager says the entry can connect.

feature_notes: present(entry:model:) opens entry.keysURL in the browser first, builds MCPKeyPanelView with .presentedChrome() and .environment(model), measures height with the view framed at width 380, reuses the existing panel if any, replaces its contentViewController, sizes it to 380 x max(height, 100), positions it top-right of NSScreen.main's visible frame (skipped if there is no main screen), starts the Escape monitor and calls orderFrontRegardless() (the panel shows without activating the app).

Escape handling: `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown)` sees every keyDown dispatched to any window of the app, not only the panel; guard `self.panel?.isVisible == true, event.keyCode == 53` else return event. So while the panel is visible, Escape pressed in the main window also closes the panel and is swallowed (`return nil`); other key events pass through. The monitor is installed at most once and removed on close. A Windows port that handles Escape only in the panel window would differ.
Window buttons close, miniaturize and zoom are hidden because the panel closes from its own xmark and on Escape.

On appear the first field (entry.fields.first?.key) is focused. Pressing Return (.onSubmit) saves only when canConnect(entry). `.onChange(of: model.mcp.state(for: entry.id).isConnected) { _, isConnected in if isConnected { onDone() } }` fires only on a change (no initial: true), so an entry already connected when the panel is presented does not auto-close; only a later transition to true calls onDone().
save() calls model.mcp.connect(entry) and closes the panel immediately, without waiting for the connection result.
pickPath: for entry.id == "filesystem" only directories can be chosen, otherwise only files; single selection; on .OK writes url.path as the draft.
Field values read model.mcp.value(for:of:) and write model.mcp.setDraft(_:for:of:).
